Figure S1. Schematic of the porous carbon synthesis process using (a) dry b) wet method

2
Figure S2. SEM images of porous carbon samples (a-c) SSC-Blank-800, (d-f) SSC-Na2S2O3-1.5-800 
and (g-i) SSC-Na2S2O3-KCl-1.5-3.6L-800. The surface of blank sample is smooth without 
micropores developed. Porous carbon synthesized by sodium thiosulfate shows higher pore 
formation. Adding KCl into the synthesis mixture increases micropores formation.

3
Figure S3. Raman spectra for the activated carbons synthesized by trisodium citrate, potassium 
carbonate, and sodium thiosulfate at 850 ℃. Higher graphitization degree was demostrated by using 
potassim carbonate. More structural defects were introduced into the porous carbon structure leading 
to more surface area.

4
Figure S4. Cyclic voltammogram comparison at 200 mV sec-1 in 6M KOH in two electrode system of 
SSC-Na2S2O3-1.5-800 and SSC-Na 2S2O3-KCl-1.5-3.3-800 with different binders. Electrodes with 
PTFE binder showed significantly higher capacitance.
